chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), who said:

Indeed, al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام), when that which came upon him came upon him, called his eldest daughter Fatimah bint al-Husayn (عليه السلام), and handed to her a wrapped book and an outward will. And 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) was suffering from an abdominal illness among them, and they saw nothing except that he was overcome by what was with him. So Fatimah handed the book to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام). Then, by Allah, that book came to us, O Ziyad.

He said: I said, "What is in that book? May Allah make me your ransom." He said: "In it, by Allah, is whatever the children of Adam need from when Allah created Adam until the world passes away. By Allah, in it are the prescribed legal punishments, even the compensation for a scratch."

key_terms.أَرْشَ: Monetary compensation or indemnity for injury.
key_terms.الْحُدُودَ: Prescribed legal punishments and penal rulings.
key_terms.الْخَدْشِ: A scratch; a minor bodily injury for which compensation is specified.
key_terms.كِتَابًا: A written book containing entrusted knowledge and rulings.
key_terms.مَلْفُوفًا: Wrapped, indicating the book was physically enclosed or secured.
key_terms.وَصِيَّةً: A manifest bequest or testamentary charge.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the transmission of the Imam's book and knowledge from Imam al-Husayn to Imam Zayn al-'Abidin (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the transfer of a written trust and manifest وصية from Imam al-Husayn (عليه السلام) to Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) through Fatimah bint al-Husayn (عليه السلام) at the time of Imam al-Husayn’s final moments. It emphasizes the continuity of divinely entrusted knowledge within the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام), and states that the book contains all that humanity needs, including detailed judicial rulings.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Al Jaroud, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup>, when it presented to him<sup>asws</sup> what which presented (death), called his<sup>asws</sup> eldest daughter Syeda Fatima<sup>asws</sup> Bint Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> handed over the wrapped Book and the apparent bequest. And it was so that Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was with a stomach illness. The ones with him<sup>asws</sup> were not seeing except that he<sup>asws</sup> was with it. So Syeda Fatima<sup>as</sup> handed over the Book to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, then, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, that Book came to be to us<sup>asws</sup>, O Zayd’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘What is in that Book? May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Therein, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is whatever the Children of Adam<sup>as</sup> would be needy to, since Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created Adam<sup>as</sup> up to the annihilation of the world. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! In it are the legal punishments, to the extent that in it is the compensation of the scratch’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu al-Jarud from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“When al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.) was about to leave this world he called his eldest daughter, Fatima and gave her a sealed document and openly before the people his directive will. Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) was ill with some internal illness and the people would see as dying. Fatima then gave the document to Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.). Thereafter, that document, by Allah, came to us, O Ziyad.”

The narrator has said that he asked the the Imam (a.s.). “What is in that document, May Allah take my soul in service for your cause?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “In it there is all that the children of Adam needed from the day Allah created Adam to the end of the world. In it there is the law of penalties and even the rules of compensation for an scratch on a victim’s body.”
